editorial.tldr: This thread was regrouped from a speculative-decoding run into a broad bucket of 77 papers and posts sharing the phrase "large language", mostly arXiv, from Nov 6. Its largest strands are hallucination fixes, which moved from preference alignment to decode-time methods, eval-validity papers, and RAG and agent-memory designs.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 26: Dev-Mem, a Show HN tool, gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode a local SQLite store of past decisions and failed approaches, a day after Merlin-Bench found 10 frontier LLMs struggle to produce verifier-accepted proofs.
editorial.why_it_matters: The useful signal for platform teams is in two strands: RAG citations can misstate provenance undetected, and eval scores move with rater drift and prompt framing, so both retrieval attribution and regression evals need their own checks.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before trusting RAG citations, sample answers and check that the cited passage actually supports the claim; when a regression eval moves, re-score an older baseline with today's judges or rubric first to rule out rater drift.
